Codex PASS lacked valid task or source evidence for every premise. PASS for the exact scoped intrinsic nef-and-big theorem, relative to the task’s actual-ample G0 grant. Historical verdicts supply no grant. This verdict does not close original P16.5 or establish the separately excluded section-volume equality. Passage −1 records the task grant; it is excluded from the external-premise array. Primary versions checked were BJ1801.08229v4, BE1805.01016v3, Fujino–Miyamoto2101.00806v1 and Stacks01Q3. Complete pertinent statements and proofs were checked, with their application hypotheses. Mathematical typography is normalized in the quotations.

132 and the genuine cone: the finite-continuous-FS intersection construction establishes genuine nef membership, decreasing closure and normalized compactness without using the disputed abstract Lemma4.6. Given two shifted continuous majorants, a smaller ample class and strictly smaller shift permit a compact-cover comparison and a common later approximant. Threshold refinement also works at poles. Bounded genuine inputs belong to one actual ample E1 cone; only their restrictions to X^lin enter ambient E~1. Remark7.16 therefore creates no illicit identification of the entire intrinsic cone with the ambient space. The published height and measure constructions retain the actual model component multiplicities, raw mass V and canonical zero. Signed metric expansion gives uniform total-variation bounds for varying perturbation coefficients. Continuous nef compatibility uses differences of continuous ample metrics and BE; Remark7.23 itself remains within its ample domain. Supporting inequalities pass through the ample perturbations, and bounded sup-norm continuity supplies both continuous-obstacle derivative signs.

133: bounded Borel strict-winning locality transfers through exact restricted measure polynomials and coefficient extraction, rather than weak convergence through indicators. For normalized u, the omitted floor mass is at most (n+1)(−E_theta(u))/k, and the full floor operator has total-variation error at most twice that quantity. Increasing winning restrictions consequently define a Radon operator of full raw mass on the original carrier. Mixed-height monotonicity and concavity give cross-integrability of every intrinsic E1 test. The ordered I bound and relative-J Holder estimate give uniform weight tails tending to zero. They establish fixed-test and simultaneous-floor weighted total-variation convergence without placing unbounded endpoints in ambient E~1.

134: fixed-floor continuity proves decreasing energy continuity, including extended energy values. With an intrinsic E1 endpoint, the uniform floor error proves arbitrary decreasing-net operator convergence against every original continuous test. Simultaneous floors transfer the numerical identities, strict concavity, quasi-triangle inequality and Holder estimates. For fixed intrinsic weights, convergence of bounded-floor integrals and the constant-weight application of Lemma7.22 give weighted weak convergence; uniform tails finish the unbounded weight. Decreasing intrinsic weights have an additional positive total-variation error tending to zero. Finite polarization establishes positive common-theta mixed products and arbitrary decreasing intrinsic-E1-weighted mixed net convergence. Mixed winning locality and domination by the top product of the average identify the same full-mass mixed floor construction. Continuous majorants and shifted envelopes pass both supporting quotient inequalities to every intrinsic base. Fixed-floor sup-distance continuity, followed by the uniform floor estimate, proves M_theta(P_theta(u+tf))→M_theta(u) on full C0 and therefore both outer derivatives. The outer energy equals envelope energy by the same majorant passage.

135: on each bounded interval, the perturbation-height coefficients have uniform bounds of order k epsilon. Ample energy usc thus passes to bounded nef energy; the infimum over continuous divisorial floor maps gives intrinsic energy usc and compact normalized cost sublevels. The actual positive mixed expansion proves C(au)≤2^(n+1)a²C(u). A decreasing convex-series contradiction gives uniform target integrability on the unit cost sublevel whenever every intrinsic E1 test is integrable. Scaling then proves finite dual energy; the converse follows immediately from a test with infinite negative integral. Every constructed output has finite dual energy. Applying the dual inequality to a fixed small contraction proves coercivity. Raw and probability-normalized duals differ by the factor V.

Corrected136: bounded integration by parts gives Cap_theta{a≤−t}≤n/t for every normalized genuine a, without a finite-energy assumption. Nested expanding convex chord majorants make chi(a) genuine and preserve exactly its pole set. Strict-winning locality, equal masses and positive mixed expansion retain the t^n factor in the floor-energy criterion. For alpha<1/(n+1), the resulting tail t^(−1/alpha) is integrable, so chi(a) has finite intrinsic floor energy. Outputs and finite-dual targets consequently give every genuine pole set zero mass. Corollary2.26 supplies the PL difference representation; the withdrawn assertion that both small signs are psh is not used. Fixed bounded divisor-floor differences, Holder control and uniform polar tails also justify the conditional full-continuous-observable conclusion for I-Cauchy cost-bounded families.

137: divisorial section-growth bounds make every finite atomic target integral a bounded continuous finite-coordinate functional on the normalized genuine cone. Compact cost sublevels and energy usc give an actual intrinsic maximizer. Both derivative signs and the obstacle inequality yield the raw equation against every original continuous direction. Divisorial Dirac solutions, together with four-point Holder control, show that I=0 forces equality at every divisorial coordinate. Common-ample all-point determination then gives equality everywhere, including poles and nondivisorial points. Equal metric measures imply I=0. Thus atomic attainment and all-point uniqueness/separation hold for every positive-mass actual nef L without a decomposition hypothesis.

138: rational effective approximation of theta−epsilon h, openness of the ample cone, smooth Cartier divisors and numerical ampleness establish an actual decomposition L=A+D. Section multiplication gives sigma and the actual bundle identity eta=(phi+epsilon sigma)/(1+epsilon). Its floor is continuous rational PL and genuinely theta-psh; it need not be finite fixed-L FS, so semiampleness is not inferred. Rational continuous FS majorants and generic normalizations converge in a common actual ample class Omega. Increasing r_epsilon has divisorial endpoint zero; the increasing pairing theorem gives strong ample convergence despite its persistent value on Z. Addition is first justified in 2Omega. Signed mixed expansion then gives Omega energy convergence, and squeezing proves strong Omega convergence of the PL floors. Only after this step does signed metric expansion give theta energy and I convergence. Decreasing continuous-net integration follows from compact Radon regularity and continuous majorants. The scalar r_epsilon passage uses countable bounded convergence outside Z and cofinal squeezing. Intrinsic floors then provide full PL maximizing approximation with bounded costs and the required target-integral convergence.

The bounded integration-by-parts estimate is independent of the energies and of the divisor-floor level k. Passing the divisor-floor differences using pole-zero outputs yields the uniform PL estimate, hence the quadratic outer error for both signs. Maximizing output measures therefore converge to the actual target first on PL and then on all C0. Midpoint strict concavity and four-point Holder control give the uniform numerical target comparison on cost sublevels. Intrinsic PL approximation extends it to every intrinsic test. Each PL model output is a finite component Dirac measure with the original multiplicities, so its integral functional is a continuous divisorial-coordinate sum. The comparison makes target integration their uniform limit on each cost sublevel. Coercivity, compactness, energy usc and target-integral continuity establish attainment for every intrinsic finite-dual-energy Radon probability target. Both C0 derivatives give M_theta(u)=V nu;137 gives uniqueness modulo constants on the entire original analytic space. A,D,H are proof auxiliaries absent from the preconstructed operator and dual.

The ancillary zero-mass cases in the supporting arguments have zero positive bounded products and zero energies, hence zero floor operators and derivatives; no uniqueness is asserted there. Arbitrary-net passages use genuine decreasing continuity, uniform floor estimates or compact Radon continuous-net integration. No monotone-convergence theorem for arbitrary Borel nets is used.

Harmless corrections and clarifications: X^lin is only the ambient pairing restriction; finite distance at common poles means the global floor bounds. In7.21 the weighted height identity subtracts the zero-weight height from the tested height. The final locality reference in7.40 is to7.21(ii), not the scaling assertion7.19(iii). The Dirichlet products have degree n−1; the telescoping sum in7.30 starts at j=0, and its test slot is (0,test). The quasi-triangle endpoint in3.31 is (phi3,phi2). The square-root Dirichlet bounds in3.33 give b_{j+1}≲b_j+sqrt(B b_j), preserving the stated exponent; n=1 follows directly from Cauchy–Schwarz. Polarization in7.34 carries 1/(n+1)!. Component classes and counts in7.36 are read as used in its proof; the equal-class application here satisfies those hypotheses. The7.38 height has all n+1 factors, including theta0. The absolute-value identity in9.19 and difference expansion in BE8.6 require minus signs. These corrections follow from the displayed definitions and proofs and require no new nonample argument.
premises: For projective X, N1(X) is finite-dimensional; Amp(X) is open and convex, Nef(X) is its closure, and Psef(X) is the closed cone generated by effective real Cartier divisors, with Big(X) its interior.

On a complete normal variety over an algebraically closed field, an R-Cartier divisor L is ample iff L^dim(Z)·Z>0 for every positive-dimensional integral closed subvariety Z. In particular ampleness of rational line bundles is numerical (Fujino–Miyamoto, Theorem1.4).
For a projective scheme X, an ample invertible sheaf A and a coherent sheaf F, F tensor A^m is globally generated for every sufficiently large integer m (Stacks01Q3).

For projective X over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, PL(X) is generated over Q by flag-ideal functions and is uniformly dense in real continuous functions on X^an. For any actual ample rational A, H(A) spans PL(X) (BJ2.1–2.3,2.25–2.26).

For projective X over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, ambient E~1 consists of differences of ample E1 potentials restricted to X^lin. The energy height extends uniquely to a symmetric multilinear pairing on (N1(X)×E~1)^(n+1), compatible with PL heights and continuous along decreasing nets in one ample E1 cone. It is increasing in genuine psh inputs with nef classes (BJ7.12,7.14–7.15).

For projective n-dimensional X over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, tuples (theta_i,u_i) in N1(X)×E~1 have unique multilinear signed Radon products of mass (theta_1…theta_n). They are positive for nef classes and genuine psh inputs, continuous along decreasing nets in a common ample E1 cone, and integrate ambient E~1 tests with the height identity. PL model coefficients are ord_F(X_0) times the component mixed intersection degree (BJ7.18–7.19).
For projective X over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, ample omega and a,b in E1(omega), 1_{a>b}MA_omega(max(a,b))=1_{a>b}MA_omega(a) on the Borel strict-winning set (BJ7.40).

For projective X over an algebraically closed trivially valued field and ample omega, normalized energy and MA on E1(omega) satisfy the mixed energy-difference identity, supporting energy inequalities, nonnegative Dirichlet identities, I/(n+1)≤J_b≤nI/(n+1), and a dimension-dependent quasi-triangle inequality. For t in [0,1], e((1−t)a+tb)−(1−t)e(a)−te(b)≥c_n t(1−t)I(a,b), c_n>0 (BJ7.27–7.28).

For projective X over an algebraically closed trivially valued field and ample omega, four E1 inputs satisfy |∫(a−a′)(MA(b)−MA(b′))|≤C_n I(a,a′)^alpha I(b,b′)^(1/2) max(J(a),J(a′),J(b),J(b′))^(1/2−alpha), alpha=2^(−n). Also |J_b(a)−J_b(a′)|≤C_n I(a,a′)^alpha max(J(a),J(a′),J(b))^(1−alpha), with dimension-only constants (BJ7.30–7.31).

For irreducible projective X over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, finitely many fixed ample classes omega_i with omega_i≤t omega_j admit Holder continuity of mixed heights on normalized E1 inputs: height differences are bounded by C_n t^(n^2) max_i d_omega_i(u_i,u_i′)^beta times max_i(d_omega_i(u_i,0),d_omega_i(u_i′,0))^(1−beta), for beta in (0,1] depending only on n (BJ7.34).

For irreducible projective X over an algebraically closed trivially valued field and fixed ample omega, addition of two normalized E1(omega) potentials is strongly continuous into E1(2omega); the Dirichlet distance of sums has a Holder bound in the component distances and bounded component costs, with dimension-only constants (BJ7.36).

For irreducible projective n-dimensional X over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, a fixed ample omega, arbitrary fixed numerical theta_0,…,theta_n, and increasing nets u_ij in E1(omega) converging on X^div to u_i in E1(omega), the n+1-factor mixed heights converge to the endpoint height (BJ7.37–7.38).

For irreducible projective X over an algebraically closed trivially valued field and ample omega, strong convergence in E1(omega) is divisorial weak convergence plus energy convergence, equivalently I_omega(u_j,u)+|sup u_j−sup u|→0 (BJ12.1–12.4).

For irreducible projective X over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, every divisorial valuation v has finite section-growth constant T_A(v) for an actual ample rational A; every normalized A-psh potential satisfies −T_A(v)≤u(v)≤0 (BJ1.28,4.46).

For a compact Hausdorff K, positive Radon measures mu_j converging weakly to mu, and increasing nonnegative lsc functions f_j, if f_j is mu_j-integrable, f=lim f_j is mu-integrable, and ∫f_j dmu_j→∫f dmu, then f_j mu_j converges weakly to f mu (BJ7.22).
For smooth connected projective X over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, if char(k)=0 or dim(X)≤2, every nef numerical class has the genuine usc envelope property (BJ5.20).

On a projective variety over a complete non-Archimedean field, including a trivially valued field, psh metrics on semiample rational line bundles are psh-regularizable. Continuous regularizable psh metrics admit uniformly continuous mixed Radon products; multilinearity extends these to continuous difference-of-psh metrics as signed products, compatible with model intersection products (BE7.14,8.4–8.7,8.18).

For projective X over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, ambient E~1∩PSH(omega)=E1(omega) when omega is ample; for nef theta, ambient E~1∩PSH(theta) is contained in the intrinsic class defined by finite bounded-floor heights (BJ7.13,Remark7.16).
